statement: Let m = len(boxes) and n = len(warehouse). For each room index i with 0 <= i < n define cap(i) = max( min{ warehouse[j] | 0 <= j <= i }, min{ warehouse[j] | i <= j < n } ). The function returns a result r, and r is the largest integer k with 0 <= k <= min(m,n) for which there exist k distinct box indices b_1,...,b_k in [0,m) and k distinct room indices q_1,...,q_k in [0,n) such that boxes[b_t] <= cap(q_t) for every t = 1..k. For k=0 no indices are needed.
preconditions: boxes and warehouse are nonempty slices of 64-bit integers with len(boxes), len(warehouse) <= 100000 and every element in [1, 10^9].

statement: For every input satisfying the preconditions, the function returns a result; it does not fail, panic, or overflow.
preconditions: boxes and warehouse are nonempty slices of 64-bit integers with len(boxes), len(warehouse) <= 100000 and every element in [1, 10^9].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, 0 <= r <= min(len(boxes), len(warehouse)).
preconditions: boxes and warehouse are nonempty slices of 64-bit integers with len(boxes), len(warehouse) <= 100000 and every element in [1, 10^9].

statement: For each room index i with 0 <= i < len(warehouse), define cap(i) = max( min{ warehouse[j] | 0 <= j <= i }, min{ warehouse[j] | i <= j < len(warehouse) } ). Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 0 if and only if for every box index b with 0 <= b < len(boxes) and every room index i with 0 <= i < len(warehouse), boxes[b] > cap(i).
preconditions: boxes and warehouse are nonempty slices of 64-bit integers with len(boxes), len(warehouse) <= 100000 and every element in [1, 10^9].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = min(len(boxes), len(warehouse)).
preconditions: boxes and warehouse are nonempty slices of 64-bit integers with len(boxes), len(warehouse) <= 100000 and every element in [1, 10^9]. Also, for every box index b and every room index j, boxes[b] <= warehouse[j].

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 1 if there exists a box index b with 0 <= b < len(boxes) and boxes[b] <= warehouse[0], and r = 0 otherwise.
preconditions: boxes and warehouse are nonempty slices of 64-bit integers with len(boxes), len(warehouse) <= 100000 and every element in [1, 10^9]. Also len(warehouse) = 1.

statement: For each room index i, define cap(i) = max( min{ warehouse[j] | 0 <= j <= i }, min{ warehouse[j] | i <= j < len(warehouse) } ). Whenever the function returns a result r, r = 1 if boxes[0] <= max_{0 <= i < len(warehouse)} cap(i), and r = 0 otherwise.
preconditions: boxes and warehouse are nonempty slices of 64-bit integers with len(boxes), len(warehouse) <= 100000 and every element in [1, 10^9]. Also len(boxes) = 1.

statement: Let r be the result of the function on (boxes, warehouse) and r' the result on (boxes', warehouse). Whenever both calls return, r = r'.
preconditions: boxes, boxes', and warehouse are nonempty slices of 64-bit integers satisfying the problem constraints. len(boxes') = len(boxes), warehouse is the same, and for every integer h in [1, 10^9], the number of occurrences of h in boxes equals the number of occurrences of h in boxes'.

statement: Let r be the result of the function on (boxes, warehouse) and r' the result on (boxes, warehouse'). Whenever both calls return, r = r'.
preconditions: boxes and warehouse are nonempty slices of 64-bit integers satisfying the problem constraints. Let warehouse' be defined by warehouse'[i] = warehouse[len(warehouse)-1-i] for every 0 <= i < len(warehouse).

statement: Let r be the result of the function on (boxes, warehouse) and r' the result on (boxes', warehouse). Whenever both calls return, r' >= r.
preconditions: boxes and boxes' are nonempty slices of 64-bit integers satisfying the problem constraints, and warehouse is a nonempty slice satisfying the problem constraints. len(boxes') = len(boxes) + 1, len(boxes') <= 100000, and boxes' is obtained from boxes by adding one additional value v with 1 <= v <= 10^9, up to permutation of the resulting multiset.

statement: Let r be the result of the function on (boxes, warehouse) and r' the result on (boxes', warehouse). Whenever both calls return, r' <= r + 1.
preconditions: boxes and boxes' are nonempty slices of 64-bit integers satisfying the problem constraints, and warehouse is a nonempty slice satisfying the problem constraints. len(boxes') = len(boxes) + 1, len(boxes') <= 100000, and boxes' is obtained from boxes by adding one additional value v with 1 <= v <= 10^9, up to permutation of the resulting multiset.

statement: Let r be the result of the function on (boxes, warehouse) and r' the result on (boxes, warehouse'). Whenever both calls return, r' >= r.
preconditions: boxes, warehouse, and warehouse' are nonempty slices of 64-bit integers satisfying the problem constraints. len(warehouse') = len(warehouse), and warehouse'[i] >= warehouse[i] for every 0 <= i < len(warehouse).

statement: For each room index i, define cap(i) = max( min{ warehouse[j] | 0 <= j <= i }, min{ warehouse[j] | i <= j < len(warehouse) } ). Whenever the function returns a result r, r = min( len(boxes), the number of room indices i with 0 <= i < len(warehouse) and cap(i) >= h ).
preconditions: boxes and warehouse are nonempty slices of 64-bit integers satisfying the problem constraints. There is a value h in [1, 10^9] such that boxes[b] = h for every 0 <= b < len(boxes).

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r = min( the number of box indices b with 0 <= b < len(boxes) and boxes[b] <= H, len(warehouse) ).
preconditions: boxes and warehouse are nonempty slices of 64-bit integers satisfying the problem constraints. There is a value H in [1, 10^9] such that warehouse[i] = H for every 0 <= i < len(warehouse).

statement: For each room index i, define cap(i) = max( min{ warehouse[j] | 0 <= j <= i }, min{ warehouse[j] | i <= j < len(warehouse) } ). Whenever the function returns a result r, if r > 0 then there exist r distinct box indices b_1,...,b_r and r distinct room indices q_1,...,q_r such that boxes[b_t] <= cap(q_t) for every t = 1..r.
preconditions: boxes and warehouse are nonempty slices of 64-bit integers with len(boxes), len(warehouse) <= 100000 and every element in [1, 10^9].

statement: Let cap(i) = max( min{ warehouse[j] | 0 <= j <= i }, min{ warehouse[j] | i <= j < len(warehouse) } ) for 0 <= i < len(warehouse). Let b[0] <= ... <= b[m-1] be the multiset of boxes sorted nondecreasing, and c[0] <= ... <= c[n-1] be the multiset { cap(i) } sorted nondecreasing, where m = len(boxes) and n = len(warehouse). Whenever the function returns r, r = max{ k | 0 <= k <= min(m,n) and for all t with 0 <= t < k, b[t] <= c[n-k+t] }.
preconditions: boxes and warehouse are nonempty slices of 64-bit integers with len(boxes), len(warehouse) <= 100000 and every element in [1, 10^9].

statement: Let H = min{ warehouse[i] | 0 <= i < len(warehouse) } and let q be the number of box indices b with boxes[b] <= H. Whenever the function returns r, r >= min(q, len(warehouse)).
preconditions: boxes and warehouse are nonempty slices of 64-bit integers with len(boxes), len(warehouse) <= 100000 and every element in [1, 10^9].
